correctness.rationale: The relative operator identity is evaluated on all four independent basis triples. For a general operator with R(e1)=a e1+u, the W-component forces a scalar trilinear defect Q to vanish whenever u is nonzero. The induced alternating form on W/Ku then forces trace(B)=0 and rank(B)<=1, whence sigma2(A)=0, contradicting Q(e2,e3,e4)=sigma2(A)+lambda with lambda nonzero. Thus u=0 is necessary. Conversely on u=0 exactly the single determinant equation remains, and h is free. Irreducibility follows because det A and sigma2(A)+lambda are coprime, making the equation primitive linear in a. Counting separates the quadratic fiber M and simple-zero eigenvalue fiber H, with full Gauss-sum and kernel/image decomposition justifications. The actual standalone program symbolically reconstructs the identity and exhaustively confirms all 65536 ambient F2 matrices, the F3 and F5 quadratic fibers and the F4 fibers; the proof, not these finite tests, handles arbitrary fields.

value.rationale: The specific four-dimensional 3-Lie algebra is the natural smallest central-derived example singled out in the originating nonzero-weight theory. The published work provides only selected projections, while the new theorem classifies every map without assuming the derived line is preserved, identifies an irreducible operator hypersurface and establishes a sharp nonzero-versus-zero-weight structural boundary. Exact finite-field arithmetic detects a non-obvious odd-characteristic square-class jump (two q^7 operators) and supplies zeta functions across every extension field. This gives a reusable complete test case for relative 3-Lie Rota–Baxter geometry, arithmetic, and deformation studies, not an arbitrary narrow invariant or a routine substitution.
